sources.title: WCAG 2.2 Understanding SC 4.1.3: Status Messages
sources.released_version_or_commit: WCAG 2.2; explanatory page updated 2026-05-11; rolling page
sources.locator: SC 4.1.3, Intent, status-message examples, Other uses of live regions or alerts, Sufficient Techniques, Failures
sources.observed_operation: web search and direct page open
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: When content changes without focus/context change and conveys success/result, waiting, progress, or errors, programmatic status semantics allow assistive technologies to present it without focus. The page cautions about excessive chatter and notes that this criterion does not require authors to generate new statuses. role=status is a sufficient technique for status/progress in listed situations; alert use is scoped to important/error cases.
sources.applicability: Pending validation and save status, async errors, and avoiding focus theft. It does not prescribe announcing every keystroke or each internal state transition.

access_window_utc.note: Reviewer direct-open/find batch window; the browser did not expose a per-page retrieval timestamp.

critic_recheck.observed_operation: Direct page open and targeted find/open of the cited locator; primary source independently checked in critic stage.
critic_recheck.review_note: Rechecked the criterion and explanation. Confirms programmatic status without focus, intent to avoid unnecessary interruption, and that the criterion does not require authors to generate a status for every change. The page does not itself make the draft’s specific excessive-chatter warning; APG S05 does.

sources.title: WCAG 2.2 Understanding SC 3.3.1: Error Identification
sources.locator: SC 3.3.1; intent; user-agent native HTML form validation discussion; ARIA21 and ARIA19 techniques
sources.observed_operation: web search and direct page open
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: If an input error is automatically detected, identify the item and describe the error in text. The explanation says native browser messages can be generic/transient/small when zoomed and may expose only the first of several errors; evaluate browser/AT support.
sources.applicability: Use textual field errors and a find-all mechanism; do not rely on color or a generic browser bubble alone.

critic_recheck.observed_operation: Direct page open and targeted find/open of the cited locator; primary source independently checked in critic stage.
critic_recheck.review_note: Rechecked input-error scope and native-validation caveats. The page defines input errors around omitted user information or a user value outside format/allowed values, and says browsers generally focus the first native invalid field; it does not prescribe that as the component’s only submit-recovery policy.

sources.title: WCAG 2.2 Understanding SC 3.3.3: Error Suggestion
sources.observed_operation: web search and direct page open
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: When an error is automatically detected and a correction suggestion is known, provide it unless doing so would jeopardize security or the purpose of the content.
sources.applicability: Server validation errors should explain the unavailable choice and, when permitted, offer current allowed choices or an actionable next step.

sources.title: WAI Forms Tutorial: User Notification
sources.locator: In-line feedback, After submit, On focus change
sources.observed_operation: web search and direct page open
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Recommends inline explanations and, on an unsuccessful form submission, focus on the first invalid input. It also shows an assertive live-region example for focus-change validation; this is an example, not a mandate for all asynchronous events.
sources.applicability: Supports an explicit submit/commit error-summary path and field-linked inline text. The assertive example is tempered by S01 and S05 for less urgent or frequent asynchronous results.

critic_recheck.review_note: Rechecked the notification page. It recommends a top-of-form linked error list and field associations, shows a dynamic alert example, and gives blur validation as an option for suitable inputs. It does not prescribe first-invalid focus after submit.

sources.title: WAI-ARIA APG Alert Pattern
sources.locator: About This Pattern; WAI-ARIA Roles, States, and Properties
sources.observed_operation: web search and direct page open
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Dynamic alerts announce important messages without interrupting; they must not affect keyboard focus, should not disappear too quickly, and frequent interruptions can harm usability.
sources.applicability: Do not move focus on individual async replies; avoid transient alerts and uncontrolled per-field announcement bursts.

critic_recheck.observed_operation: Direct page open and targeted find/open of the cited locator; primary source independently checked in critic stage.
critic_recheck.review_note: Rechecked alert guidance: alerts must not affect keyboard focus, should not disappear too quickly, and frequent interruptions inhibit usability.

sources.applicability: Keep stable tab order and meaningful summary links as errors/status are inserted, including under reflow.

sources.title: WCAG 2.2 Understanding SC 1.4.10: Reflow
sources.locator: SC 1.4.10; Adjusting content into a single column; Resize Text overlap; Focus Not Obscured overlap
sources.observed_operation: web search and direct page open
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Typical reading content should reflow to a 320 CSS pixel viewport and vertical reading; the page notes 200% text enlargement under SC 1.4.4 and exceptions for content whose meaning/function needs two-dimensional layout.
sources.applicability: Error summary, labels, messages, and field groups must wrap in narrow and zoomed layouts; target form content is ordinary service text, not an identified exception.

critic_recheck.review_note: Rechecked reflow conditions: ordinary vertical content at 320 CSS pixels, with exceptions for content requiring two-dimensional layout. 200% text enlargement is a useful separate proposed check, not the reflow threshold itself.

sources.applicability: Use direction-aware structure and test bidirectional layout. This source says nothing about translation quality or compatibility with specific assistive technologies.

sources.title: RFC 9110: HTTP Semantics
sources.locator: §13.1.1 If-Match; §13.2.2 evaluation of preconditions; §15.5.13 412 Precondition Failed
sources.observed_operation: web search and direct page open
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: If-Match is evaluated with strong entity-tag comparison and is commonly used on state-changing requests to prevent lost updates. A false condition means the method is not performed and may produce 412; a server may return success if it can determine the same change already succeeded.
sources.applicability: Use a canonical entity version/ETag on save. Treat 412 as conflict requiring refresh/review while preserving local dirty text. RFC does not specify the portal's product conflict UI or idempotency design.

access_window_utc.note: Reviewer direct-open/find batch window; the browser did not expose a per-page retrieval timestamp.

critic_recheck.observed_operation: Direct page open and targeted find/open of the cited locator; primary source independently checked in critic stage.
critic_recheck.review_note: Rechecked RFC 9110 §§13.1.1, 13.2.2, 15.5.13: If-Match uses strong comparison; false precondition means the method is not performed and may yield 412; success is permitted where the same state-changing request is known to have already succeeded.

sources.locator: Validation; Constraint validation; Server validation; Schema validation; Localization; Form libraries

sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Guide documents native constraints, custom/realtime validation, server field errors supplied through validationErrors, which clear after the user modifies the field. sources.applicability: Maintained reference for field semantics and validation API. It does not document stale-request identity, multi-reviewer concurrency, save interruption reconciliation, multilingual testing, or a target-toolkit choice.
